=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:267-271 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: Space-separated numeric push arguments immediately before redirects are treated as file descriptors and removed from the push arguments.
  WHY: `git push origin 2 > /dev/null` can be checked as a push to the checked-out branch rather than branch `2`, bypassing the guard for the actual destination.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:262-272, 432-455 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The root guard can drop the actual refspec when `--repo` is used and can treat a numeric argument before a redirect as a refspec.
  WHY: The guard may inspect the checked-out branch or branch `2` instead of `feature/x`, allowing a push without checking its actual destination.
- tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py:998-1038 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The byte-for-byte guard-copy parity assertion fails because `.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` and `workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py` diverge.
  WHY: The CI parity test fails, and consumer repos can receive guard behavior that differs from the root implementation.
- tests/test_audit_plans_command.py:29-30 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `test_template_parity` fails because the root `audit-plans.md` command differs from its template copy.
  WHY: The test asserts byte-for-byte equality, so the mismatch fails CI.
- tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py:901-923 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: `test_push_parser_guards_real_destination` includes cases for push argument handling that the root guard does not support.
  WHY: Four parametrized cases fail in CI, causing `tests-hooks-and-orchestrator` to fail.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:_evaluate_bash, `if target.warning.startswith("could not resolve git push refspec")` branch (line ~1311-1314 in the post-diff state) | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Confirmation is requested only for warnings starting with the exact string `could not resolve git push refspec`, not for the longer warning prefix.
  WHY: Pushes taking the longer-warning path fall through without the new confirmation flow, producing inconsistent behavior.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:_push_targets `if destination == "HEAD":` block | severity=high | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Resolving `HEAD` to the current branch before the push creates a time-of-check/time-of-use race if another process checks out a different branch before the push.
  WHY: The guard may block or allow based on a branch different from the one the push writes.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:_evaluate_bash branch introducing `_request_confirmation("could not resolve git push refspec source; verify the actual push destination and source tip")` | severity=high | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: An unresolved push source now triggers a permission prompt instead of the previous warn-only fallback.
  WHY: Ambiguous push commands, including pushes in detached-HEAD situations, can now require operator acknowledgement without a documented contract change.
- tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py:test_numeric_redirects_do_not_hide_refspecs and test_unresolved_push_refspec_requires_confirmation | severity=critical | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: New test cases expect redirect-parsing and unresolved-refspec behavior that the divergent guard implementations may not consistently provide.
  WHY: The cases can pass or fail depending on which guard copy is loaded, and CI reports test failures.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:262-272 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The root guard lacks the redirect handling described by the README and agents documentation.
  WHY: The documentation describes distinguishing `git push origin 2>/dev/null` from `git push origin 2 > /dev/null`, but the root guard has no `redirect_target` logic and the parity test requires both guards to match.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
